title: Establish what the Standard XII is actually worth in Dutch terms (HAVO vs VWO)
duration_realistic: 1 day of desk work, but must happen before any shortlist is built
what_happens: Dutch admission is decided against Dutch school-leaving levels, not against percentages. Nuffic's India country module compares a CBSE All India Senior School Certificate with a pass in 5 relevant subjects to a HAVO diploma, and only to a VWO diploma if the student has A1, A2 or B1 in 5 relevant subjects. An ISC (CISCE) certificate reaches VWO only with an average of at least 75% in 5 relevant subjects. VWO-comparable is the entry ticket to a research university (WO) bachelor; HAVO-comparable opens universities of applied sciences (HBO) only. State board Standard XII sits at HAVO at best.
the_trap: Counselors read a 92% CBSE aggregate as 'strong' and shortlist research universities. The Dutch test is not an aggregate - it is the grade band in five relevant subjects. A student with one C1 among the five relevant subjects is HAVO-comparable, and every WO bachelor in the country is closed to them regardless of aggregate. Diagnose this in month one, not after the rejection.
exact_quote: All India Senior School Certificate from the CBSE - a HAVO diploma if obtained with a pass in 5 relevant subjects; a VWO diploma if obtained with an A1, A2 or B1 in 5 relevant subjects.

title: Pick the right sector: research university (WO) or university of applied sciences (HBO)
duration_realistic: 1-2 weeks of shortlisting
what_happens: The two sectors are legally different, not a ranking. WO bachelors are 3 years and need VWO-comparable prior education; HBO bachelors are 4 years (including placements) and need HAVO-comparable prior education. An Indian student who is only HAVO-comparable has three honest routes: an HBO bachelor, an HBO propedeuse followed by a transfer into WO year 1, or a foundation/preparatory year run by the institution. There is no appeal route that converts a HAVO-level diploma into WO admissibility on the strength of a high aggregate.
the_trap: Selling HBO as 'the backup' rather than the correct destination. HBO is the larger sector, is where most English-taught applied programmes sit, and is fully covered by the same IND student permit. Mis-sold, the student rejects a valid offer and loses the intake.
exact_quote: Standard XII diploma from a state board with a pass in 5 relevant subjects - a HAVO diploma.

title: Check the university's own country rule - some accept only CBSE and CISCE
duration_realistic: 1 day, per university on the shortlist
what_happens: Dutch institutions publish country-specific admission rules that are stricter than the Nuffic comparison. TU Delft, for example, accepts a Standard XII (academic stream) from CBSE with at least B1 per subject, or from CISCE with at least 75% per subject, and explicitly refuses other Indian boards. Each shortlisted programme must be checked individually; the rule sits on the institution's own admission pages, not on Studielink and not on Study in NL.
the_trap: Assuming Nuffic's comparison is the admission rule. It is not - Nuffic itself says a credential evaluation is not legally binding and institutions decide their own admissions. A Maharashtra or Karnataka state-board student can be HAVO-comparable per Nuffic and still be refused outright by the university's own board list.
exact_quote: Certificates from other Indian Boards do not qualify for admission.

title: Match the subject requirements at VWO level (Mathematics B, Physics, Chemistry)
duration_realistic: 1 day, but can force a subject re-sit costing a full year
what_happens: Beyond the diploma level, most technical and science programmes demand named subjects at Dutch pre-university (VWO) level - typically Mathematics B, and depending on the programme Physics, Chemistry or Biology. TU Delft publishes a 'diploma with additional requirements' page listing which subjects each BSc needs. Indian students taking a commerce or biology stream are frequently short of Mathematics B equivalence for engineering and computer science.
the_trap: Subject shortfalls are discovered in March, after Studielink has been filed. Remedies (a certified maths module, an institutional entrance exam, or a foundation year) have their own earlier deadlines, so the fix is only available to students who checked in the autumn.
exact_quote: Mathematics should always be a Final examination subject. Depending on the BSc programme of your choice, Physics, Chemistry, Biology should also be Final examination subjects.

title: Book and sit the English language test
duration_realistic: 4-8 weeks: 2-4 weeks to a test slot, plus ~13 days to results
what_happens: English-taught programmes require an accepted test. Study in NL lists Cambridge English (B2 First, C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency), IELTS, LanguageCert, Pearson, TOEFL iBT and TOEIC as the tests institutions generally accept. Minimum scores are set per institution: TU Delft requires IELTS Academic 6.5 overall or TOEFL iBT 90 for English-taught programmes. Some institutions exempt applicants whose prior education was taught in English, but most Dutch universities do not extend that exemption to Indian boards.
the_trap: Counting on a medium-of-instruction letter from an Indian school in place of a test. Exemptions are institution-specific and rarely cover Indian secondary education. The test is also the item most likely to breach a university's separate document deadline, because scores post ~13 days after the sitting.
exact_quote: IELTS 6.5 (Academic version, Overall Band Score); TOEFL 90 (internet based).

title: Decide whether a Nuffic/IDW credential evaluation is needed at all (usually it is not)
duration_realistic: 10 working weeks if ordered - which is why most students should not order one
what_happens: Nuffic, via the IDW counter, issues formal credential evaluations comparing a foreign diploma to a Dutch one. For undergraduate admission this is almost never required: Dutch institutions run their own assessment and can request an evaluation themselves if they need one. Order it only if a specific institution asks for it in writing, or if the qualification is unusual and not listed in Nuffic's India module.
the_trap: Ordering a credential evaluation 'to be safe' and then waiting ten working weeks for a document nobody asked for, while the real application deadline passes. The inverse trap also exists: treating the evaluation as proof of admission when Nuffic states it is not.
exact_quote: A credential evaluation is not legally binding. This means that Dutch universities and universities of applied science determine themselves which students they admit.

title: Create the Studielink account and file the enrolment application (this is step one, not the university form)
duration_realistic: 1-2 hours to file; open from roughly 1 October
what_happens: Studielink is the national enrolment portal for Dutch higher education and the enrolment application there is what creates the student's record at the institution. Dutch residents must log in with DigiD; an applicant living abroad is explicitly exempt and uses a Studielink username and password instead. Filing in Studielink does not by itself constitute an application to the programme - the institution is then triggered to invite the student into its own admission system. The national deadline for non-fixus bachelor programmes is 1 May at 23:59, but institutions set earlier practical deadlines for non-EU applicants.
the_trap: Two symmetrical mistakes. First, filing only in Studielink and assuming the application is complete - the university's own document dossier is a separate submission. Second, filing only in the university's portal and never touching Studielink, which leaves the student unenrollable even after admission. Also note Studielink is not universal: some institutions register students from abroad by another route, so confirm before assuming.
exact_quote: Only if you are not eligible for a DigiD because you are not an official resident of the Netherlands, will you be able to continue to use your old Studielink username and password.

title: TRAP STEP: if the programme has a numerus fixus, the deadline is 15 January and nothing moves it
duration_realistic: The decision to target a fixus programme must be made by October; the door shuts 23:59 CET on 15 January
what_happens: A numerus fixus (capped) programme has a national application deadline of 15 January at 23:59 CET, filed through Studielink. It is not an advisory date and no institution can waive it - it is a statutory capacity procedure. The programmes most Indian students want are disproportionately fixus: at TU Delft, Computer Science and Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Architecture, Clinical Technology and Nanobiology are numerus clausus; at the UvA, Business Administration, Economics and Business Economics, Political Science and Psychology (English tracks) are fixed-quota. A student may enter a maximum of two numerus fixus programmes per academic year, and only one for Medicine, Dentistry, Dental hygiene or Physiotherapy.
the_trap: This single date kills more Indian intakes than the visa ever does. The counselling season in India peaks after Standard XII board results in May - seven months too late for a fixus programme. A student who discovers in March that TU Delft Computer Science closed on 15 January has lost the entire year: there is no late round, no waitlist entry, no appeal. Check fixus status of every shortlisted programme in September/October of the year BEFORE the intake.
exact_quote: until 23:59 on 15 January for numerus fixus programmes

title: Submit the institution's own document dossier and pay its application fee
duration_realistic: 2-4 weeks to assemble; decision typically within 8 weeks of a complete file
what_happens: After the Studielink enrolment application the institution invites the student into its own online application system, where diplomas, transcripts, the English test certificate and a CV are uploaded. Institutions charge their own non-refundable application fee - TU Delft charges EUR 100 for BSc applicants with an international diploma. TU Delft allows one BSc programme per academic year, plus one backup programme for numerus clausus applicants, and states it will respond within 8 weeks of a complete application. Incomplete files are simply not processed.
the_trap: Missing the institution's own deadline, which for non-EU applicants is usually earlier than the national 1 May. TU Delft's non-fixus deadline is 1 April at 23:59 CEST with all documents uploaded; the UvA's advisory deadline for international prior education is also 1 April and it warns that after that it cannot guarantee visa and housing procedures will finish in time. A file that is complete on 30 April is, in practice, a file that missed the intake.
exact_quote: Applicants are required to pay a non-refundable EUR 100 application fee. You will be informed about the payment method in the online application.

title: Numerus fixus selection, ranking number on 15 April, and a two-week clock to accept
duration_realistic: 15 January to 15 April for selection, then exactly 2 weeks to accept
what_happens: If applications exceed places, the institution runs its own selection between 15 January and 15 April. Every applicant receives a ranking number through Studielink on 15 April. A student inside the capacity is offered a place and must accept it in Studielink within two weeks or it is reassigned automatically. Students outside capacity can still be pulled up if offered places are declined, notified by email. If a fixus programme is undersubscribed, all applicants are offered a place on 15 April - and still must accept within two weeks.
the_trap: The two-week acceptance window falls in late April, when Indian Standard XII board exams are in full swing and students are off email. An unaccepted place is not held: it goes automatically to the next ranking number. Diary the window at the point the application is filed in January, and give the university a second contact address.
exact_quote: If you are offered a place, you have to accept this place via Studielink within two weeks. If you don't accept the place within two weeks, your place will be assigned to another student automatically.

title: Get Indian documents apostilled by the Ministry of External Affairs
duration_realistic: 2-6 weeks depending on state-level attestation before MEA
what_happens: The IND requires official foreign documents used in an application to be legalised. India is an apostille country, so the route is an apostille from the Indian Ministry of External Affairs, usually preceded by state-level attestation (HRD/GAD/SDM) depending on the document type. Documents already in English do not need translation for use in the Netherlands; only Hindi (or other non-English) documents need a sworn translation into Dutch, English, French or German. The IND itself does not legalise or translate anything and warns the process is slow.
the_trap: Paying an agent for sworn translations of documents that are already in English - unnecessary cost and delay. The real trap is the opposite direction: starting the apostille only after admission, when the university needs the legalised passport copy and birth certificate to file the IND application in May or June. Start it in parallel with the application, not after the offer.
exact_quote: To use a document from India in the Netherlands, you must have it legalised with an apostille by the Indian Ministry of External Affairs.

title: Budget the institutional tuition fee, not the statutory one
duration_realistic: Decide before applying; the fee is fixed for the whole degree
what_happens: The Netherlands has two tuition fees. The statutory fee (wettelijk collegegeld) is EUR 2,694 for 2026-2027 and is only available to EEA, Swiss and Surinamese nationals who have not already taken a comparable Dutch degree. Everyone else pays the institutional fee (instellingscollegegeld), which Study in NL puts at EUR 9,000 to EUR 20,000 a year for a bachelor's. The exact figure is set per programme by the institution and is published on the programme page.
the_trap: Indian families budget from the EUR 2,694 headline that dominates 'cheap Europe' listicles and discover the real number after admission. For a four-year HBO bachelor the difference is roughly EUR 25,000 to EUR 70,000 over the degree. Price the institutional fee for every shortlisted programme at shortlist stage, not at offer stage.
exact_quote: The annual tuition fee (statutory fee) is EUR 2,694 for the academic year 2026-2027. [...] For students with other nationalities the average tuition fee for bachelor's programmes is between EUR 9,000 and EUR 20,000.

title: Meet the IND study norm: 12 x EUR 1,130.77 for 2026
duration_realistic: Funds must be in place and documented before the institution files, typically April-June
what_happens: For a study residence permit the IND requires proof of enough money to live and study for 12 months. The 2026 study norm for higher professional education (hbo) and university is EUR 1,130.77 per month, valid 1 January to 31 December 2026, which is EUR 13,569.24 for the year. The norm explicitly excludes tuition fees. Accepted proof includes the money sitting in the student's own freely withdrawable account, a deposit of 12 x the study norm into the educational institution's bank account, a scholarship declaration, or a statement of financial support from a company or a private financier who holds the amount.
the_trap: Every supporting bank document must be no more than 3 months old at the time it is used, so funds parked in January are stale by May. The second trap is a fixed deposit or instrument that cannot be freely withdrawn - the IND accepts certificates of deposit only if they state the money may and can be withdrawn. Note also the 2027 study norm is not published as of 14 September 2026; do not quote a 2027 figure to a family.
exact_quote: Study amounts 2026. These amounts are valid from 1 January 2026 up to and including 31 December 2026. Higher professional education (hbo) or university - EUR 1,130.77.

title: Transfer tuition AND the living-cost guarantee to the university before it will touch the visa file
duration_realistic: The money has to leave India in April-June for a September start
what_happens: In practice Dutch universities do not let students prove funds independently - they require the money in the university's own account first, because the university is the one filing with the IND. TU Eindhoven requires non-EEA admitted students to transfer a guarantee fee (the tuition prepayment) plus a proof-of-financial-means amount it states as EUR 13,600 for 2026, and says it begins the visa and residence permit arrangements only once both are received. The living-cost portion is refunded after enrolment, once the student has opened a Dutch bank account. TU Delft sets its full payment deadline at 1 July for a September start.
the_trap: Two money traps. First, the timing: an Indian family clearing the LRS route, arranging an education loan and doing a ~EUR 27,000 international transfer in June has almost no margin before the university's payment deadline - start the banking conversation in March. Second, note the figures do not match: IND's 2026 norm is EUR 13,569.24 (12 x EUR 1,130.77) while TU/e asks for EUR 13,600. Universities round up and add their own buffer; always pay the university's stated figure, not the IND arithmetic, and never send a short amount because bank transfer charges were deducted en route.
exact_quote: For 2026, the IND has set this amount at EUR 13,600 per year, excluding tuition fees and visa application costs. [...] TU/e will begin your visa and/or residence permit arrangements only after receiving: Full guarantee fee, Proof of financial means, Required visa documents.

title: Apply for scholarships on their own, earlier calendar
duration_realistic: Deadlines typically 1 February to 1 May, ahead of admission decisions
what_happens: The main nationally funded option for non-EEA students is the NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship), worth EUR 5,000 paid in the first year only; it is financed by the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with participating institutions, and is explicitly not a full-tuition scholarship. Closing dates and eligible fields are set by each participating institution. India also has the Orange Tulip Scholarship run by Nuffic Neso India with institution-specific awards. Most institutional scholarships require an admission application to already be on file.
the_trap: Scholarship deadlines usually sit before or on top of the admission deadline, and the UvA warns explicitly that scholarship deadlines may be earlier than its application deadline. A student who waits for an offer before looking at funding has already missed the round. Also: a partial scholarship does not remove the proof-of-funds obligation - the balance still has to be transferred.
exact_quote: The scholarship amounts to EUR 5,000. You will receive this in the first year of your studies. Please note that this is not a full-tuition scholarship.

title: Check the institution is an IND recognised sponsor - if it is not, there is no student permit
duration_realistic: 10 minutes, but do it before accepting an offer
what_happens: Only an IND-recognised sponsor can file a study residence permit. The IND maintains a monthly-updated public register of recognised sponsors with a separate register for the Study category. All publicly funded Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences are on it; small private colleges, language schools and some 'pathway' providers may not be. If the institution is not a recognised sponsor, no study residence permit can be filed for the student at all.
the_trap: Private institutions and agent-marketed 'foundation programmes' are where this bites. A student can hold a genuine admission letter from an unrecognised provider and still have no immigration route. Check the Study register by name before any money moves.
exact_quote: A recognised sponsor is a company, school, or organisation that has been recognised by the IND. A recognised sponsor can apply for a residence permit for, for example, employees, au pairs or students.

title: The university - not the student - files the MVV and residence permit together (TEV)
duration_realistic: Filed May-July; legal decision period 60 days, in practice often 2-4 weeks
what_happens: This is the structural difference from Germany, the UK or Australia: there is no student visa appointment to book and no visa application for the student to fill in. The IND states plainly that only the educational institution can apply for a residence permit for the student, and it applies for the MVV (entry visa) and the student residence permit at the same time - the combined TEV procedure. The fee is EUR 254.00 for study at all education levels, usually invoiced to the student by the university. The IND must decide within 60 days. What the student actually does is narrow: hand the university a valid passport copy, the legalised documents, the signed TB declaration of intent, the income appendix, and the money - then wait.
the_trap: Counselors who run a Netherlands file the way they run a UK or US file waste weeks hunting for a visa application form and a VFS appointment that do not exist, and worse, they let the student go quiet after admission. The student's job post-offer is to answer the university's immigration office within 24 hours, every time. A single unanswered document request stalls the file, and the file cannot be escalated by the student because the student is not the applicant.
exact_quote: Only this educational institution can apply for a residence permit for you.

title: Sign the TB declaration of intent - India is not on the exemption list
duration_realistic: 5 minutes to sign; the test itself happens within 3 months of arrival
what_happens: Indian nationals must undergo a tuberculosis test. The IND's exemption appendix (form 7644, valid from 30 May 2025) lists the nationalities that are excused - it includes China, Sri Lanka, the UAE and most of Europe and the Americas, but it does not include India. The student signs the Appendix 'Declaration of intent to undergo a TB test' (form 7603), which the university encloses with the application, and then takes the referral form (7604) to the municipal health service (GGD) after arrival.
the_trap: The test is a condition of the permit, not a formality. The IND grants the permit on the express condition that the student actually takes the test within three months of receiving it, and says failure to do so may result in cancellation of the permit. Students settle into term, forget the GGD appointment, and put their legal residence at risk in month four.
exact_quote: You are granted this permit under the express condition that you will actually undergo a TB test within three months after having received your residence permit.

title: Collect the MVV sticker in India: 3-month window, New Delhi, Mumbai or Bangalore
duration_realistic: Book the moment approval lands; up to 10 working days to get the passport back
what_happens: Once the IND approves, the student has 3 months to apply for the MVV visa sticker at the Dutch embassy in New Delhi or the consulates-general in Bangalore or Mumbai - and may use any of the three regardless of which one the IND letter names. For a student whose sponsor applied, the email from the educational institution containing the V number is accepted instead of a photocopy of the IND decision letter. The passport is surrendered at the appointment and returned with the sticker in up to 10 working days, either collected in person or couriered by DTDC for INR 850 per airway bill. The MVV is a Type D sticker, multiple-entry, valid for the whole Schengen area.
the_trap: Appointment scarcity, not eligibility, is what breaks this step. NetherlandsWorldwide warns outright that because of the high number of applicants, appointments fill up quickly. Between the appointment wait and the 10 working days without a passport, a student who books casually in late July will not be in Delft for the September intro week. Book the slot the same day the university forwards the approval.
exact_quote: Make your appointment in good time. After receiving the letter from the IND informing you of its positive decision, you have 3 months to apply for an MVV visa sticker.

title: Collect the residence permit card at the IND Student Days in Utrecht
duration_realistic: One Saturday, late August or September, by appointment only
what_happens: The residence permit is a physical card collected after arrival. For students the IND runs central handover days (centrale uitreikdagen) at the Jaarbeurs Beatrix Building in Utrecht - for the 2026 intake these were Saturday 29 August 2026 and Saturday 19 September 2026. The educational institution sends the notification containing the appointment link and a colour code; the student books a slot, brings the appointment code and the passport, and receives the card. Students who cannot attend either date make an appointment at a regular IND desk afterwards.
the_trap: Two things fail here. First, students turn up without an appointment or without the passport, and the IND will not hand over the document. Second, the handover dates are fixed and few - a student who lands on 20 September has missed both 2026 dates and falls back to the ordinary IND desk queue, which delays the BSN appointment and the bank account, which in turn delays the refund of the living-cost deposit. Land before the last Student Day.
exact_quote: You can only collect your residence document on one of these two dates. You need to make an appointment. The notification from your educational institution will tell you how to do so.

title: Secure housing before departure - this is a gating step, not a lifestyle detail
duration_realistic: Start the month the offer arrives; 3-6 months of searching is normal
what_happens: Dutch students do not live on campus; they rent rooms in shared houses across the city. Study in NL states the country is dealing with a severe housing shortage, that there is not enough student housing for everyone, and that accommodation must be arranged before arriving in the Netherlands. Some institutions reserve a limited number of rooms for first-year international students, usually allocated first-come on a portal that opens in spring. Average rent is around EUR 550 a month, higher in Amsterdam and Utrecht. The official advice on scams is blunt: never sign a tenancy contract without having seen the room, and do not pay brokerage fees.
the_trap: Housing is not a soft step - it is the address that BRP registration depends on, and BRP registration is what produces the BSN, which produces the bank account, which produces the refund of the living-cost deposit. No address means the whole arrival chain stalls. Students who decline university-arranged housing because it looks expensive frequently end up in hostels into October. If the institution offers a guaranteed room, take it.
exact_quote: Be aware that the Netherlands is dealing with a severe housing shortage. There is not enough student housing to accommodate everyone. That's why it's very important to arrange your housing as soon as possible.

title: Register in the BRP at the municipality within 5 days and get the BSN
duration_realistic: Appointment within the first week; BSN issued at the appointment
what_happens: Anyone living in the Netherlands for more than 4 months must register as a resident in the Personal Records Database (BRP) at the municipality of their address, within 5 days of arrival, and receives a citizen service number (BSN) at that appointment. The BSN is required to open a bank account, take out health insurance, or take a job or internship. Most universities run intake days where the municipality registers international students on campus. A legalised (apostilled) birth certificate is normally required at registration. A municipality may only refuse registration on three grounds: no valid passport or European ID, no lawful residence, or no intention to stay longer than 4 months.
the_trap: Arriving without an apostilled birth certificate. It cannot be fixed from the Netherlands in any reasonable time - it means sending documents back to India for MEA apostille while the BSN, and therefore the bank account and the deposit refund, sit blocked. The second trap is municipal waiting times, which NetherlandsWorldwide itself flags as longer than usual: book the appointment before flying, and take the university intake-day slot if one is offered.
exact_quote: You must register within 5 days of arriving in the Netherlands. [...] You will be given a citizen service number (BSN) when you register.

title: Take the TB test at the GGD within 3 months of receiving the permit
duration_realistic: One appointment, 30 minutes; must fall inside the 3-month window
what_happens: After collecting the residence document, the student books an appointment with the municipal health service (GGD) and brings the TB referral form (IND form 7604), partly completed in advance. The test is normally a chest X-ray. The result is sent to the IND. This is the only immigration step in the whole chain that the student performs personally and unsupervised, which is exactly why it gets forgotten.
the_trap: The three-month clock runs from receipt of the residence permit, not from arrival, and the IND says failure may result in cancellation of the permit. A student who collects the card at the Utrecht Student Day in early September must have been tested by early December - in the middle of first-term exams. Book the GGD appointment in the same week as the BRP appointment.
exact_quote: Should it become clear after the issue of a residence permit that - despite signing the declaration of intent - you failed to undergo a TB test within the period of three months, this may result in a cancellation of the permit that was granted.

title: Get the health insurance right - and redo it the day a part-time job starts
duration_realistic: Before departure for the private policy; within days of any job offer for the Dutch one
what_happens: The Dutch rule is counter-intuitive. A student in the Netherlands for study purposes only is legally not allowed to take out Dutch public health insurance and must instead hold a home-country policy with sufficient cover or a private international student policy. The moment the student takes a part-time job, Dutch public health insurance becomes compulsory and must start on the first day of work. Paid internships follow a separate test: a non-EU student on an internship is insured under the Wlz scheme if paid at least the Dutch minimum wage, and board and lodging count as remuneration.
the_trap: The switch is the trap, not the initial policy. Students take a 10-hour campus job in second term, never change insurer, and are uninsured under Dutch law from day one of that job - which surfaces later as a CAK letter and a fine. Conversely, families waste money trying to buy Dutch basic insurance before arrival, which is not permitted while no decision has been taken on the residence permit.
exact_quote: You are legally not allowed to take out a Dutch public health insurance if you are in the Netherlands for study purposes only. [...] You are required to have a Dutch public health insurance if you have a (part-time) job.

title: Open a Dutch bank account and reclaim the living-cost deposit
duration_realistic: 1-3 weeks after the BSN; refund a few weeks after that
what_happens: With a BSN and a registered address the student opens a Dutch current account. The university then refunds the proof-of-financial-means amount it was holding - TU Eindhoven refunds the full amount after enrolment and after a Dutch bank account has been opened, and warns it may take a few weeks before the money is accessible. TU Delft similarly refunds living costs after deducting the permit and housing fees, roughly three weeks after the programme starts.
the_trap: Families budget as if the EUR 13,600 is spent, or as if it comes back on day one. Neither is true: it is the student's own money, but it is locked from roughly May until October. The first term must be funded separately. Tell families this at the point they make the transfer, not when the student runs out of cash in week three.
exact_quote: The full amount will be refunded after enrollment and after opening a Dutch bank account. Please note: it may take a few weeks before you can access the refunded amount.

title: Stay compliant: 50% of credits a year, and 16 work hours a week with a TWV
duration_realistic: Ongoing, assessed every study year
what_happens: The student residence permit runs for the duration of the studies plus 3 months, to a maximum of 5 years, and only for as long as the conditions are met. The binding condition is academic: the student must obtain at least 50% of the credits for each study year, and the institution assesses progress annually and reports insufficient progress to the IND. On work, a student may do at most 16 hours a week during the year, or full-time in June, July and August but not both, and in every case the employer must hold a work permit (TWV) from the UWV. After graduating, a former student can apply for the one-year orientation year permit to look for work.
the_trap: Two live risks. First, a student who fails first year badly does not merely repeat the year - the institution reports it and the permit can be withdrawn. Note this sits on top of the Dutch binding study advice (BSA), which can force a student off the programme entirely. Second, students take cash-in-hand or unpermitted work believing the 16-hour cap is the only rule; without a TWV the work is illegal regardless of hours, and the Labour Inspectorate checks.
exact_quote: The student residence permit is valid for the duration of the studies plus 3 months, with a maximum of 5 years and only as long as international students meet the requirements. For example, they must obtain at least 50% of their credits each year.
